concepts.title: Stress and Strain
concepts.definition: A deforming force applied to a solid is measured as stress -- force per unit area -- while the resulting relative change in shape or size is strain, a dimensionless ratio such as extension over original length. Solids resist deformation because their atoms sit in fixed equilibrium positions connected by spring-like bonds.
concepts.key_idea: Stress is the cause (force per area), strain is the effect (fractional deformation) -- the pairing defines elasticity.

concepts.title: Hooke's Law and the Stress-Strain Curve
concepts.definition: For small deformations stress grows in direct proportion to strain -- Hooke's law -- and the constant of proportionality is the modulus of elasticity. Beyond that linear region the curve bends: the elastic limit passes, plastic flow begins, and eventually the material reaches its fracture point at the ultimate tensile strength.
concepts.key_idea: Below the elastic limit stress over strain is a fixed number (the modulus); beyond it the deformation stops undoing itself.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph201.txt lines 161-260 (sections 8.3 Hooke's law, 8.4 stress-strain curve, elastic limit, yield point, permanent set, fracture)

solution_steps.explain: Within the linear region, doubling the load doubles the extension -- stress over strain stays constant.
The straight part ends at the proportional limit; the elastic limit lies nearby, then yield, then work hardening up to ultimate strength and fracture.
Brittle materials snap soon after the linear region; ductile ones stretch far through plastic flow before breaking.

concepts.title: Young's Modulus of a Wire
concepts.definition: Young's modulus is the ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain -- the stiffness of a material against stretching. For a wire of cross-section area and original length pulled by a force through an extension, dividing the stress by the strain evaluates it numerically.
concepts.key_idea: Stress over strain -- a big modulus means a stiff material that barely stretches under heavy load.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph201.txt lines 261-360 (section 8.5 elastic moduli, Young's modulus, experimental determination, steel versus copper examples)

Divide the extension by the original length.
Stress over strain is Young's modulus.

concepts.title: Bulk Modulus and Shear Modulus
concepts.definition: Solids and fluids resist squeezing too: the bulk modulus is pressure change divided by the fractional volume change it causes. Resistance to shape change is captured by the shear modulus, the ratio of shearing stress to the angle-like strain it produces; liquids, which flow, have essentially no shear modulus.
concepts.key_idea: Bulk modulus guards volume, shear modulus guards shape -- a liquid protects volume but surrenders shape.

concepts.title: Elastic Potential Energy in a Stretched Wire or Spring
concepts.definition: Work done to deform an elastic body is stored as elastic potential energy. For a spring of stiffness k stretched by x the stored energy is half k x squared, and the same half-times-stress-times-strain structure gives the energy density of any stretched wire.
concepts.key_idea: Elastic deformation banks energy -- half the stiffness times the square of the stretch -- ready to be released on unloading.

Half the spring constant times the squared stretch is the stored energy.
